target: OAW's own command-line tools at claude/oaw-2 80bb3fa (scripts/oaw.py and the helper scripts it installs into a project), exercised offline as a user would: no network, no model calls

categories.B1: non-ASCII input: emoji (up to 1,000 of them), CJK, combining marks or right-to-left text in a name, path, title or file content
categories.B2: very long, empty or malformed input: a huge argument or file, a blank value, broken JSON or YAML, an unexpected type
categories.B3: interrupted or partial operation, then recovery: a step stops midway (a missing file, a killed run, a read-only file) and the next run must recover or report clearly
categories.B4: state consistency across commands: what one command writes, another reads differently (list after add or remove, status after a change, a record that disagrees with the files)
categories.B5: repeated runs: running the same command twice duplicates, corrupts or wrongly refuses
categories.B6: error reporting: a wrong exit code, a silent failure, a success message for a failed step, or a misleading message
categories.B7: paths: spaces, relative paths, a different working directory, a symlink, or a file where a folder is expected
categories.B8: user data: a user's own file overwritten, deleted or lost without consent

seeded_defect_rules: one defect per defect journey, critical or major, from a different category where possible; at least four of B1, B2, B3, B4 among the six
a defect is a small source change to OAW (a patch), observable through the command line on the journey's path or an input variation a careful tester could try
each defect has a mechanical oracle: an existing OAW regression test, or a new deterministic check, that fails with the patch and passes without it
no comment, name or message in the patch may hint at the defect
half the defects are written by one author session and half by another
